The Dojo

A dojo, not a gym

Shotojuku is a family-oriented, multigenerational dojo. Grandparents, parents and four-year-olds have all begun on this floor — and many who started as children now teach on it. The line of teachers is unbroken, and it reaches all the way back to the founder of Shotokan himself.

All members are taught by Shihan Kai Leung and his staff of experienced adult black belts, in a clean, friendly, fully equipped facility near the subway. Over 40 classes run every week, and membership is unlimited — train as often as you like, at your level.

Whether you come for focus and discipline for your child, or for the traditional and sport sides of karate yourself, the first step is the same: one class, on the house.

Japan Karate-Do USA Shotokai · International Shotokai Federation HQ · Miyazaki O.B. Kai · NY Traditional Karate League

Programs

Four scrolls, unrolled

Children and adults train in separate classes, and every level trains at its own pace. Pick your scroll — the first class on it is free.

Kids build focus, discipline, respect and confidence alongside real karate — basics, forms and controlled sparring, taught with patience. Many of our students start as young as four, and many of today's instructors started exactly here.

Shotokan Karate 松濤館

基本・型・組手

How training works

The path from white belt to black belt

Students start as white belts and earn their way to black belt over several years of steady training. Every class is built on three pillars:

基本

Kihon

Basics

The fundamentals — stances, strikes, blocks and kicks — drilled until power and focus become instinct. Rigorous physical training is the foundation of the Shotokan style.

型

Kata

Forms

Set sequences of technique against imagined opponents. The Kenkojuku style taught here preserves the traditional self-defense applications inside every form.

組手

Kumite

Sparring

Partner work and sparring, including WKF-style sport kumite — where timing, distance and control come together under pressure, safely and progressively.

One belt at a time

Progress is earned in the open, test by test. Parents watch it happen; adults feel it happen. The belt is the receipt — the focus, discipline and confidence are the real promotion.

系 船越から梁へ

Lineage

An unbroken line of teachers

Shotojuku's teaching descends directly from the founder of Shotokan. That lineage isn't a slogan — it's who corrects your stance in class.

Gichin Funakoshi

Founder of Shotokan

Brought karate from Okinawa to mainland Japan and founded the Shotokan school, with his third son, Gigo Funakoshi.

Tomosaburo Okano

Kenkojuku Founder

Direct disciple of both Funakoshi masters; his Kenkojuku dojo preserved the traditional self-defense heart of the style. Later named a living national treasure for karate by the Japanese government.

Toyotaro Miyazaki

Brought Shotokan to New York

A top student of Master Okano who came to America in 1967 and taught the original style in New York — founder, with Shihan Leung, of this dojo in 1982.

Kai Leung

Shihan · Master Instructor

Master Miyazaki's highest-ranked disciple and best-known instructor — still on the floor at Shotojuku, teaching every generation himself.

Shihan Kai Leung began training in 1964, earned his black belt in 1967, and has taught since the early 1970s. A tournament champion in his own right — Top Ten ranking by Karate Illustrated in 1982, and winner of the 1984 All-American Open Championships at Madison Square Garden — he became Master Miyazaki's highest-ranked disciple.

He taught the karate instructor certificate program at Long Island University for over fifteen years, co-authored the textbook Karate: Martial Art and Sport, and is a founding member and chief instructor of the International Shotokai Federation — headquartered at this dojo. His students have become national and international champions, teachers, and — just as often — parents who bring their own kids back to train.

  • 1964

    Shihan Leung begins martial arts training; introduced to Goju-ryu by his older brother, Master Kwok Leung.

  • 1967

    Earns his black belt. The same year, Master Miyazaki arrives in America.

  • 1978–82

    Assistant instructor at Master Miyazaki's Tokutai Dojo in Flushing, after founding the Whitestone Dojo.

  • 1982

    Sent by Master Miyazaki to head the Astoria dojo — the Miyazaki Dojo, now Shotojuku, is founded.

  • 1984

    Wins the All-American Open Championships at Madison Square Garden.

  • Today

    Three generations of black belts assist Shihan in running the dojo. The annual Traditional Karate-do Invitational Championship bears his name.

Instructors

Taught by people who grew up on this floor

Shotojuku's shidoin (instructors) are Shihan Leung's own senior students — several began here as children.

梁

Shihan Kai Leung

Master Instructor

Founding member and chief instructor of the International Shotokai Federation. Teaching since the early 1970s; a scholar of martial arts history with senior students on four continents.

BC

Bernard Clemons

Instructor · Kobudo

An outstanding karate and kobudo practitioner and a career martial artist — one of the top weapons experts in the country, with many grand championships won with his weapon kata.

EN

Edward Nieto

Instructor · Team Captain

Started with Shihan at age eight. A tournament champion — gold at the 2006 USANKF Junior Olympics, bronze at the 2006 AAU Nationals — and captain of the competition team.
